picks.title: Stillness as a Superpower
picks.summary:
In a year defined by volatility, noise, and nonstop demands, I’ve learned that stillness is one of the rarest — and most powerful — skills any of us can develop. In this episode of The Stoic’s Guide Podcast, I explore Stillness as a Superpower as a tactical advantage in 2026, and why calm, deliberate thinking isn’t just helpful… it’s transformative.

Modern life is engineered to hijack your attention. Endless notifications. Emotional triggers. Algorithm‑driven urgency. The pressure to react instantly. Most people are living in a state of mental turbulence, making decisions from stress instead
picks.reason: Explores stillness as a transformative practice aligned with Stoic calm and focus.

picks.title: 369 | Gregg Caruso on Living Well Without Free Will
picks.summary: The worry about debates over free will is that they degenerate into semantics -- what do you mean by "free will," really? But there are important substantive issues that shouldn't be ignored. Do people deserve blame for doing wrong things? Can we make choices that create meaning for our lives? Philosopher Gregg Caruso denies the reality of free will, but is in favor of making good choices, as he discusses in his new book How to Live Well Without Free Will. Listen or watch Rolex Planet Visionaries wherever you get your podcasts. #ad            Blog post with transcript:  https://preposterousuni
picks.reason: Philosophical discussion on free will and moral responsibility relevant to Stoic ethics.
